views.name: track_with_album_artist_genre_media
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Track.TrackId,
  Track.Name,
  Track.AlbumId,
  Album.Title AS Title,
  Album.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  Artist.Name AS Name,
  Track.MediaTypeId,
  MediaType.Name AS Name_1,
  Track.GenreId,
  Genre.Name AS Name_2,
  Track.Composer,
  Track.Milliseconds,
  Track.Bytes,
  Track.UnitPrice
FROM Track
LEFT JOIN Album ON Track.AlbumId = Album.AlbumId
LEFT JOIN Artist ON Album.ArtistId = Artist.ArtistId
LEFT JOIN Genre ON Track.GenreId = Genre.GenreId
LEFT JOIN MediaType ON Track.MediaTypeId = MediaType.MediaTypeId

params.description: Provides one-row-per-track metadata combining Track with its Album, Album's Artist, Genre, and MediaType to answer track-level metadata and pricing queries.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve detailed metadata for individual tracks (title, album, artist, genre, media type) and track-level attributes (composer, duration, size, unit price). | Filter or group tracks by album, artist, genre, or media type while preserving track-level granularity. | Compose higher-level analytics that start from track-level rows (e.g., sales joins or aggregations) by using this view as the canonical track dimension.
params.output_schema: TrackId: unique identifier of the track — derives from Track.TrackId | Name: track name/title — derives from Track.Name | AlbumId: foreign key to the album containing the track — derives from Track.AlbumId | Title: album title (Album.Title) — derives from Album.Title | ArtistId: foreign key to the album's artist (Album.ArtistId) — derives from Album.ArtistId | Name: artist name (Artist.Name) — derives from Artist.Name | MediaTypeId: foreign key to the media type of the track — derives from Track.MediaTypeId | Name_1: media type name (MediaType.Name) — derives from MediaType.Name | GenreId: foreign key to the track's genre — derives from Track.GenreId | Name_2: genre name (Genre.Name) — derives from Genre.Name | Composer: track composer field — derives from Track.Composer | Milliseconds: track duration in milliseconds — derives from Track.Milliseconds | Bytes: file size in bytes — derives from Track.Bytes | UnitPrice: track unit price — derives from Track.UnitPrice
params.grounded_columns: Track.TrackId | Track.Name | Track.AlbumId | Album.Title | Album.ArtistId | Artist.Name | Track.MediaTypeId | MediaType.Name | Track.GenreId | Genre.Name | Track.Composer | Track.Milliseconds | Track.Bytes | Track.UnitPrice
params.metric: This view exposes no derived aggregate metrics by itself; all columns are direct base columns from Track, Album, Artist, Genre, and MediaType. | If consumers need measures, compute them on top of this view. Example derived measures that can be composed safely at track grain: | track_count = COUNT(TrackId)  -- count of tracks | total_track_duration_ms = SUM(Milliseconds)  -- sum of track durations | total_bytes = SUM(Bytes)  -- sum of track file sizes | total_unit_price = SUM(UnitPrice)  -- sum of unit prices | avg_unit_price = AVG(UnitPrice)  -- average track price
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension tables or one-row-per-key views on their respective keys — safe because this view is one-row-per-TrackId (one row per track) so joining to one-row-per-key dimensions does not duplicate measures. | Safe joins (do not duplicate this view's track-level rows/measures): |  - join to Album or album-level views ON AlbumId = Album.AlbumId (Album is 1:1 or 1:many from Album to Track; from this view's perspective Album is a 0/1 match per row). |  - join to Artist or artist-level views ON ArtistId = Artist.ArtistId (Artist is 0/1 per Album, thus 0/1 per track row). |  - join to Genre ON GenreId = Genre.GenreId (0/1 per track). |  - join to MediaType ON MediaTypeId = MediaType.MediaTypeId (0/1 per track). |  - join to sibling dimension-like views that are one-row-per-key (e.g., artist_album_counts if it is one-row-per-artist) ON the matching key — safe when the sibling view is truly one-row-per-key. | Unsafe joins (would multiply this view's rows/measures unless you re-aggregate): |  - do NOT directly join to one-to-many child tables or views (e.g., InvoiceLine, PlaylistTrack, or any invoice/playlist tables that list multiple sales/appearances per track) without first aggregating those tables to the track grain. Example unsafe joins: |    * joining invoice_line_with_invoice_customer_track (which contains invoice lines) directly will multiply track rows by invoice_line occurrences — instead aggregate invoice lines to TrackId (e.g., SUM(Quantity), SUM(UnitPrice*Quantity)) and then join to this view on TrackId. |    * joining playlist_track_with_metadata directly will duplicate track rows for each playlist membership — instead compute playlist counts per TrackId first and then join. |  - do NOT join to hierarchical or recursive outputs that produce multiple rows per artist/employee unless reduced to one row per join key. | Composition recipes: |  - To compute track sales: aggregate invoice_line_with_invoice_customer_track to track-level (GROUP BY TrackId) computing measures like total_sales = SUM(UnitPrice*Quantity) and total_quantity = SUM(Quantity), then JOIN the aggregated result to this view ON TrackId — this preserves one-row-per-track. |  - To enrich album-level reports starting from albums: aggregate this view to album grain (GROUP BY AlbumId) before joining to album-level outputs to avoid duplication. |  - To get per-artist aggregates: aggregate this view to ArtistId (GROUP BY ArtistId) or join aggregated sales (by TrackId) and then roll up to ArtistId.

views.description: Denormalized track-level relation enriched with album, artist, genre and media type metadata. Useful whenever queries need track attributes alongside album/artist names or genre/media labels (sales by track, playlist analysis, catalog listings). | Use for: List tracks with artist/album/genre labels; Filter tracks by genre or media type then aggregate sales; Join invoice lines to track metadata for sales analysis

views.name: invoice_line_with_invoice_customer_track
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  InvoiceLine.InvoiceLineId,
  InvoiceLine.InvoiceId,
  Invoice.InvoiceDate,
  Invoice.CustomerId,
  Invoice.BillingCountry,
  Invoice.Total AS InvoiceTotal,
  InvoiceLine.TrackId,
  InvoiceLine.UnitPrice,
  InvoiceLine.Quantity,
  (InvoiceLine.UnitPrice * InvoiceLine.Quantity) AS LineAmount,
  Track.Name AS Name,
  Track.AlbumId,
  Track.GenreId,
  Track.MediaTypeId
FROM InvoiceLine
LEFT JOIN Invoice ON InvoiceLine.InvoiceId = Invoice.InvoiceId
LEFT JOIN Track ON InvoiceLine.TrackId = Track.TrackId

params.description: Line-level invoice rows enriched with invoice header and track metadata, answering questions about individual invoice lines, their amounts, associated invoice/customer, and track attributes.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve or filter individual invoice lines with their invoice header (date, customer, billing country) and track attributes (name, album, genre, media type). | Compute sums/aggregates at the invoice-line grain (e.g., total revenue by customer, by invoice, by track) by aggregating this view. | Join to dimension-level entities (customer, track metadata, album, artist, genre, media type) in a cardinality-safe way to add attributes without inflating measures. | Drive downstream aggregations such as track-level sales, invoice-level totals verification, customer-level lifetime calculations when aggregated properly.
params.output_schema: InvoiceLineId: surrogate/key for the invoice line — from InvoiceLine.InvoiceLineId | InvoiceId: FK to the invoice header — from InvoiceLine.InvoiceId | InvoiceDate: date/time of the invoice — from Invoice.InvoiceDate | CustomerId: customer FK on the invoice header — from Invoice.CustomerId | BillingCountry: invoice billing country — from Invoice.BillingCountry | InvoiceTotal: total amount for the invoice header — from Invoice.Total | TrackId: FK to the sold track on this line — from InvoiceLine.TrackId | UnitPrice: unit price recorded on the invoice line — from InvoiceLine.UnitPrice | Quantity: quantity recorded on the invoice line — from InvoiceLine.Quantity | LineAmount: extended line amount = UnitPrice * Quantity — derived expression using InvoiceLine.UnitPrice and InvoiceLine.Quantity | Name: track name (title) — from Track.Name | AlbumId: FK to Track.Album — from Track.AlbumId | GenreId: FK to Track.Genre — from Track.GenreId | MediaTypeId: FK to Track.MediaType — from Track.MediaTypeId
params.grounded_columns: InvoiceLine.InvoiceLineId | InvoiceLine.InvoiceId | InvoiceLine.TrackId | InvoiceLine.UnitPrice | InvoiceLine.Quantity | Invoice.InvoiceId | Invoice.InvoiceDate | Invoice.CustomerId | Invoice.BillingCountry | Invoice.Total | Track.TrackId | Track.Name | Track.AlbumId | Track.GenreId | Track.MediaTypeId
params.metric: LineAmount = SUM(UnitPrice * Quantity) WHEN AGGREGATED at desired grain (base expression: InvoiceLine.UnitPrice * InvoiceLine.Quantity) | InvoiceTotal = Invoice.Total (invoice-level metric; when aggregating this view by invoice, use MAX(InvoiceTotal) or SUM(LineAmount) depending on intent — see composition guidance) | RowCount = COUNT(InvoiceLineId) (implicit row-level count of invoice lines)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to customer_with_supportrep or a customers dimension on CustomerId (Invoice.CustomerId = Customer.CustomerId) — safe because this view is one-row-per-InvoiceLine and Customer is one-row-per-Customer; joining adds customer attributes without duplicating invoice-line measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to track_with_album_artist_genre_media or a tracks dimension on TrackId (InvoiceLine.TrackId = Track.TrackId) — safe because track_with_album_artist_genre_media is one-row-per-Track; it will not multiply invoice-line rows and preserves LineAmount measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to album or genre or media type dimensions (e.g., AlbumId, GenreId, MediaTypeId) using the corresponding FK columns — these dimension tables are one-row-per-entity and will not duplicate invoice-line measures. | do NOT directly join to artist_album_counts, track_sales_agg, monthly_invoice_totals, customer_lifetime_value, tracks_ranked_by_sales, or other aggregate views that are many-per-key without re-aggregation — these are aggregated outputs that may be at a different grain and could duplicate or mis-align measures if joined without proper keys and aggregation. Instead, either: | - aggregate this view to the same grain as the aggregate view (e.g., sum LineAmount by TrackId) and then join on TrackId, or | - join this view to the aggregate view on keys where the aggregate view is exactly one-row-per-key (e.g., if track_sales_agg is one-row-per-TrackId, join on TrackId; verify sibling view grain before joining). | special note on InvoiceTotal: InvoiceTotal comes from the invoice header (Invoice.Total) and is constant for all lines of a given InvoiceId. If you aggregate this view by InvoiceId and want the true invoice total, use MAX(InvoiceTotal) or take the value from the invoice header directly; do NOT SUM(InvoiceTotal) across lines (that would multiply the invoice total by number of lines). | when composing to produce higher-level measures (e.g., invoice-level revenue or customer lifetime): aggregate LineAmount (SUM(LineAmount) grouped by InvoiceId or CustomerId) rather than summing InvoiceTotal from each line. Conversely, if you need invoice header attributes, join or select InvoiceTotal but avoid summing it over lines without deduplication. | joins that preserve measures without re-aggregation: any join to a true dimension (1:1 or many-to-1 from this view to dimension) on CustomerId, TrackId, AlbumId, GenreId, MediaTypeId, or InvoiceId (if invoice header is one-row-per-invoice) is safe. Joins to one-to-many children (e.g., invoices -> invoice lines reversed, playlists -> tracks) will multiply rows and must be followed by re-aggregation.

views.description: Invoice line items enriched with invoice header, customer and track metadata. Useful for revenue, customer purchase history, track-level sales, and time-based invoice analyses. | Use for: Compute revenue by track/genre/customer/date; Customer purchase history and lifetime value; Invoice reconciliation (line amounts vs invoice totals)

views.name: customer_with_supportrep
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Customer.CustomerId,
  Customer.FirstName,
  Customer.LastName,
  Customer.Company,
  Customer.Email,
  Customer.SupportRepId,
  Employee.LastName AS LastName_1,
  Employee.FirstName AS FirstName_1,
  Employee.Title
FROM Customer
LEFT JOIN Employee ON Customer.SupportRepId = Employee.EmployeeId

params.description: Provides one-row-per-customer enriched with that customer's assigned support representative (employee) basic name and title.
params.when_to_use: Fetch customer details together with their support rep's name/title for display or reporting. | Filter or group customers by attributes of their support rep (e.g., rep title) while retaining one row per customer. | Join customer-level data to other customer-level aggregates (e.g., lifetime value, invoice totals) without duplicating customer rows.
params.output_schema: CustomerId: unique identifier for the customer; derived from Customer.CustomerId | FirstName: customer's first name; derived from Customer.FirstName | LastName: customer's last name; derived from Customer.LastName | Company: customer's company name (may be NULL); derived from Customer.Company | Email: customer's email address; derived from Customer.Email | SupportRepId: identifier of the support representative assigned to the customer (may be NULL); derived from Customer.SupportRepId | LastName_1: support representative's last name (Employee.LastName) — aliased because it comes from Employee | FirstName_1: support representative's first name (Employee.FirstName) — aliased because it comes from Employee | Title: support representative's job title (Employee.Title)
params.grounded_columns: Customer.CustomerId | Customer.FirstName | Customer.LastName | Customer.Company | Customer.Email | Customer.SupportRepId | Employee.EmployeeId | Employee.LastName | Employee.FirstName | Employee.Title
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to customer-level aggregates or views on CustomerId (for example: customer_lifetime_value on CustomerId) — safe because this view is one-row-per-CustomerId so joining on CustomerId will not duplicate its rows or any customer-level measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to employee/rep dimension on SupportRepId = Employee.EmployeeId (or to employee_org_hierarchy keyed by EmployeeId) — safe because Employee is a one-row-per-EmployeeId dimension in the base schema and the LEFT JOIN in this view preserves one row per customer. | avoid joining directly to one-to-many tables/views (for example: invoice_line_with_invoice_customer_track, track_with_album_artist_genre_media, playlist_track_with_metadata) without aggregation or deduplication first — those are many rows per customer or per track and would multiply customer rows and any derived measures. | If you need to combine this view with invoice-line level or track-level detail, first aggregate the detail to CustomerId (or to SupportRepId) producing one row per CustomerId (or per SupportRepId) and then join — this preserves correct cardinality and prevents measure inflation. | If composing with sibling aggregated views (artist_album_counts, monthly_invoice_totals, track_sales_agg, tracks_ranked_by_sales, customer_lifetime_value), prefer joining on the aggregate's key (e.g., CustomerId to customer_lifetime_value) because those aggregates are already condensed; verify their grain matches CustomerId before joining. | Do NOT assume this view contains any pre-computed metrics (sums/counts). It is strictly customer-level attributes with an optional employee lookup; any metrics must be computed in a separate, cardinality-aware aggregation step.

views.description: Customer rows joined to their support representative (employee). Useful for support workload, rep performance, and customer contact listings grouped by rep. | Use for: List customers by support rep; Aggregate customers per support rep; Contact lists including rep info

views.name: artist_album_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Artist.ArtistId,
  Artist.Name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT Album.AlbumId) AS AlbumCount,
  COUNT(DISTINCT Track.TrackId) AS TrackCount
FROM Artist
LEFT JOIN Album ON Album.ArtistId = Artist.ArtistId
LEFT JOIN Track ON Track.AlbumId = Album.AlbumId
GROUP BY Artist.ArtistId, Artist.Name

params.description: Counts of albums and tracks per artist (one row per artist).
params.when_to_use: Get the number of distinct albums and distinct tracks for each artist. | Report artist catalog size (album and track counts) for dashboards and summaries. | Join artist-level catalog metrics into customer or sales analyses without re-aggregating artist measures. | As a building block for per-artist ratios or rates (e.g., tracks per album) by composing additional aggregations on top.
params.output_schema: ArtistId: the primary key identifying the artist; derives from Artist.ArtistId (base column referenced in the view). | Name: the artist name; derives from Artist.Name (base column referenced in the view). | AlbumCount: distinct count of albums belonging to the artist; derived metric COUNT(DISTINCT Album.AlbumId) where Album.AlbumId is the base column referenced. | TrackCount: distinct count of tracks belonging to the artist's albums; derived metric COUNT(DISTINCT Track.TrackId) where Track.TrackId is the base column referenced.
params.grounded_columns: Artist.ArtistId | Artist.Name | Album.AlbumId | Album.ArtistId | Track.TrackId | Track.AlbumId
params.metric: AlbumCount = COUNT(DISTINCT Album.AlbumId)  -- counts unique AlbumId for each Artist.ArtistId | TrackCount = COUNT(DISTINCT Track.TrackId)  -- counts unique TrackId for tracks whose Album.AlbumId is linked to the artist
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to artist dimension or one-row-per-artist views on ArtistId — safe because this view is one-row-per-ArtistId so its measures will not be duplicated. Example: JOIN artist_album_counts AS a ON a.ArtistId = artist_dim.ArtistId. | Do NOT directly join this view to any table or view that is one-to-many from Artist (for example, Album, Track, playlist_track_with_metadata, track_with_album_artist_genre_media) without re-aggregation, because those joins will multiply the artist rows and therefore duplicate AlbumCount and TrackCount. If you must join to a one-to-many relation, either: | - pre-aggregate the one-to-many side to one row per ArtistId before joining, or | - join inside a subquery and re-aggregate measures appropriately (e.g., SUM or MAX depending on intended semantics) to avoid double-counting. | Safe composition examples: | - Join to customer_with_supportrep or invoice-level aggregates on keys unrelated to ArtistId (e.g., join by a reporting dimension) is safe when you expect a single artist row to augment each reporting row; still be mindful if the reporting rows themselves are many-to-one to artists. | - Use this view as the left side in further GROUP BY ArtistId queries (e.g., compute TrackCount / AlbumCount) because the view is already aggregated to the artist grain. | Unsafe composition examples: | - Do NOT join artist_album_counts directly to Track or Album tables on ArtistId since Album and Track are many per artist and will multiply AlbumCount/TrackCount values. | - Do NOT join to playlist_track_with_metadata (which is many tracks per playlist) on ArtistId without re-aggregation, because playlists contain many track rows and would duplicate artist measures.

views.description: Counts of albums and tracks per artist. Useful for catalog size metrics, artist popularity baselines, and join-ready artist-level aggregates. | Use for: Catalog metrics per artist; Join artist-level aggregates to sales data; Identify artists with many/few tracks

views.name: monthly_invoice_totals
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  STRFTIME('%Y', Invoice.InvoiceDate) AS InvoiceYear,
  STRFTIME('%m', Invoice.InvoiceDate) AS InvoiceMonth,
  COUNT(Invoice.InvoiceId) AS InvoiceCount,
  SUM(Invoice.Total) AS TotalRevenue
FROM Invoice
GROUP BY STRFTIME('%Y', Invoice.InvoiceDate), STRFTIME('%m', Invoice.InvoiceDate)

params.description: Monthly totals of number of invoices and summed invoice revenue (one row per invoice year + invoice month).
params.when_to_use: Answering month-level revenue and invoice count questions (e.g., revenue by month, invoice counts by month). | Composing time-series aggregates where month/year is the grain (can be joined to dimensional date or customer summaries after joining on month/year). | Feeding month-level inputs to downstream aggregations (quarterly, yearly) by re-aggregating InvoiceCount and TotalRevenue.
params.output_schema: InvoiceYear: calendar year extracted from Invoice.InvoiceDate via STRFTIME('%Y', Invoice.InvoiceDate); identifies the year component of the invoice date. | InvoiceMonth: zero-padded month extracted from Invoice.InvoiceDate via STRFTIME('%m', Invoice.InvoiceDate); identifies the month component of the invoice date within the year (01..12). | InvoiceCount: count of invoices in that year+month; derived from COUNT(Invoice.InvoiceId). | TotalRevenue: total invoice monetary amount for that year+month; derived from SUM(Invoice.Total).
params.metric: InvoiceCount = COUNT(Invoice.InvoiceId) -- cardinality-preserving aggregate counting distinct invoice rows in the Invoice table per InvoiceYear+InvoiceMonth. | TotalRevenue = SUM(Invoice.Total) -- additive monetary measure summing the Invoice.Total values per InvoiceYear+InvoiceMonth.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a date dimension (if present) on (date_year = InvoiceYear AND date_month = InvoiceMonth) — safe because monthly_invoice_totals is one row per year+month so measures are not duplicated when enriching with a 1-to-1 date/month dimension. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to pre-aggregated monthly customer or product/month summaries (e.g., customer_monthly_agg) on (InvoiceYear, InvoiceMonth) — safe if the other view is also exactly one row per same month key, because both sides share the same grain and no duplication occurs. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many detail tables (e.g., InvoiceLine, track, playlist_track_with_metadata, invoice_line_with_invoice_customer_track) on any invoice or invoice-line key without re-aggregation, because those joins will multiply invoice-level counts and revenue. If you need to combine with row-level tables, first aggregate that detail to the same (InvoiceYear, InvoiceMonth) grain and then join. | do NOT join to views that are many-per-month (e.g., track listings, playlist items) without reducing them to one row per month; otherwise InvoiceCount and TotalRevenue will be inflated. | If composing into larger aggregates (quarter, year, running totals), re-aggregate InvoiceCount with SUM(InvoiceCount) and TotalRevenue with SUM(TotalRevenue) grouped by the new grain — these measures are additive across months. | When joining to views keyed by InvoiceYear + InvoiceMonth, ensure identical formatting/casing of InvoiceMonth (this view uses zero-padded month strings via STRFTIME('%m')). Convert the other side to the same representation or cast as needed to avoid mismatches.

views.description: Aggregated invoice totals and invoice counts by year and month. Useful for revenue time-series, period-over-period comparisons, and trend analysis. | Use for: Monthly revenue and invoice volume; Time series comparisons and seasonality

views.name: track_sales_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Track.TrackId,
  Track.Name,
  SUM(InvoiceLine.Quantity) AS TotalQuantitySold,
  SUM(InvoiceLine.UnitPrice * InvoiceLine.Quantity) AS TotalRevenue,
  COUNT(DISTINCT Invoice.CustomerId) AS DistinctCustomerCount,
  MAX(Invoice.InvoiceDate) AS LastInvoiceDate
FROM InvoiceLine
LEFT JOIN Invoice ON InvoiceLine.InvoiceId = Invoice.InvoiceId
LEFT JOIN Track ON InvoiceLine.TrackId = Track.TrackId
GROUP BY Track.TrackId, Track.Name

params.description: Per-track sales summary: total quantity, revenue, distinct buying customers, and last invoice date, at the TrackId grain.
params.when_to_use: Report total units and revenue sold per track | Rank or filter tracks by sales, revenue, distinct customer reach, or most recent sale | Join track-level sales summary to track metadata (album/artist/genre) or to downstream dashboards without duplicating measures | As a pre-aggregated building block when computing higher-level aggregates (e.g., album/artist totals) by re-aggregating this per-track view
params.output_schema: TrackId: unique identifier for the track (derived from Track.TrackId) | Name: track name/title (derived from Track.Name) | TotalQuantitySold: total number of units of this track sold across all invoice lines (derived from SUM(InvoiceLine.Quantity)) | TotalRevenue: total revenue for this track across all invoice lines (derived from SUM(InvoiceLine.UnitPrice * InvoiceLine.Quantity)) | DistinctCustomerCount: number of distinct customers who purchased this track (derived from COUNT(DISTINCT Invoice.CustomerId)) | LastInvoiceDate: most recent invoice date when this track was sold (derived from MAX(Invoice.InvoiceDate))
params.grounded_columns: InvoiceLine.InvoiceLineId | InvoiceLine.InvoiceId | InvoiceLine.TrackId | InvoiceLine.UnitPrice | InvoiceLine.Quantity | Invoice.InvoiceId | Invoice.CustomerId | Invoice.InvoiceDate | Track.TrackId | Track.Name
params.metric: TotalQuantitySold = SUM(InvoiceLine.Quantity)  -- sum over InvoiceLine.Quantity for the track | TotalRevenue = SUM(InvoiceLine.UnitPrice * InvoiceLine.Quantity)  -- sum of line price * quantity for the track | DistinctCustomerCount = COUNT(DISTINCT Invoice.CustomerId)  -- distinct customers who appear on invoices for the track | LastInvoiceDate = MAX(Invoice.InvoiceDate)  -- most recent Invoice.InvoiceDate for the track
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to track_with_album_artist_genre_media on TrackId — safe because this view is one-row-per-TrackId (TrackId is the aggregation grain) so joining to a one-row-per-TrackId dimension will not duplicate measures | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to tracks_ranked_by_sales on TrackId — safe because tracks_ranked_by_sales is also track-grain (ranking per TrackId) and will not multiply rows | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to playlist_track_with_metadata on TrackId only if you first aggregate playlist_track_with_metadata up to TrackId (for example count playlists per track) — direct join is NOT safe because playlist_track_with_metadata is one-to-many (many playlists may reference the same TrackId) and would multiply this view's measures | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to artist_album_counts only after mapping TrackId -> AlbumId -> ArtistId and re-aggregating sales upward; do NOT directly join this view to artist_album_counts on ArtistId without re-aggregation because artist_album_counts is aggregated at artist/album grain and a direct many-to-one or many-to-many join can duplicate rows/measures | do NOT join this view directly to invoice_line_with_invoice_customer_track or InvoiceLine unless you re-aggregate or restrict to a 1:1 relationship — invoice_line_with_invoice_customer_track is many invoice lines per track and will multiply sums if joined directly | when composing to produce higher-level totals (album, artist, genre): perform GROUP BY on the desired higher-level key and SUM(TotalQuantitySold), SUM(TotalRevenue), SUM(DistinctCustomerCounts) is NOT safe for DISTINCT customers — instead compute DISTINCT CustomerId from invoice_line_with_invoice_customer_track or perform a customer-level rollup (e.g., count distinct customers by track then deduplicate by customer when aggregating to artist) because COUNT(DISTINCT) does not distribute across SUM | for LastInvoiceDate when rolling up to album/artist: use MAX(LastInvoiceDate) after joining to album/artist (safe, MAX is reducible) | summary rule: safe to join to true 1:1 or many-to-1 dimensions keyed by TrackId (track metadata, ranked track lists, single-row track attributes). Avoid direct joins to one-to-many transaction-level tables/views (invoice lines, playlists) without re-aggregation to prevent measure duplication.

views.description: Pre-aggregated sales metrics per track: total quantity sold, total revenue, distinct customers, and last sale date. Useful for top-selling tracks, long-tail analysis, and inventory planning. | Use for: Top selling tracks by revenue or quantity; Customer reach per track; Recency of sales per track

views.name: playlist_track_with_metadata
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  PlaylistTrack.PlaylistId,
  Playlist.Name AS Name,
  PlaylistTrack.TrackId,
  Track.Name AS Name_1,
  Track.AlbumId,
  Album.Title AS Title,
  Album.ArtistId,
  Artist.Name AS Name_2
FROM PlaylistTrack
LEFT JOIN Playlist ON PlaylistTrack.PlaylistId = Playlist.PlaylistId
LEFT JOIN Track ON PlaylistTrack.TrackId = Track.TrackId
LEFT JOIN Album ON Track.AlbumId = Album.AlbumId
LEFT JOIN Artist ON Album.ArtistId = Artist.ArtistId

params.description: Provides one-row-per-playlist-track with denormalized metadata about the playlist, track, album, and artist — useful for questions that need track-level details within playlists.
params.when_to_use: List tracks in a playlist with track, album, and artist names | Filter or count playlist entries by album or artist | Compose further aggregations at the playlist-track grain (e.g., number of tracks per playlist, distinct artists per playlist) by aggregating this view | Join to sales or invoice aggregates keyed by TrackId or PlaylistId to attribute sales/metrics to playlist entries (with care about cardinality)
params.output_schema: PlaylistId: PlaylistTrack.PlaylistId — identifier of the playlist (grain column) | Name: Playlist.Name — playlist name (from Playlist table) | TrackId: PlaylistTrack.TrackId — identifier of the track (grain column) | Name_1: Track.Name — track name (from Track table) | AlbumId: Track.AlbumId — identifier of the album that contains the track (from Track table) | Title: Album.Title — album title (from Album table) | ArtistId: Album.ArtistId — identifier of the artist associated with the album (from Album table) | Name_2: Artist.Name — artist name (from Artist table)
params.grounded_columns: PlaylistTrack.PlaylistId | PlaylistTrack.TrackId | Playlist.Name | Track.TrackId | Track.Name | Track.AlbumId | Album.AlbumId | Album.Title | Album.ArtistId | Artist.ArtistId | Artist.Name
params.composition: Cardinality-safe joins (do NOT duplicate rows/measures): |  - Join to Playlist (dimension) on PlaylistId — safe because Playlist is one-row-per-PlaylistId and the view is one-row-per-(PlaylistId,TrackId); joining adds playlist attributes without multiplying rows. |  - Join to Track (dimension) on TrackId — safe for the same reason: Track is one-row-per-TrackId, so joining preserves the playlist-track grain. |  - Join to Album or Artist on AlbumId or ArtistId respectively — safe when joining by their primary keys because Album and Artist are one-row-per-id and therefore do not duplicate view rows. |  | Be careful / NOT safe without re-aggregation (these will multiply rows because they are one-to-many relative to the view's grain): |  - Do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables such as invoice_line or other sales line-level tables (e.g., invoice_line_with_invoice_customer_track) without aggregating those tables first to the same (PlaylistId,TrackId) or TrackId grain. Joining invoice_line (many lines per TrackId) will duplicate playlist-track rows and inflate counts/sums. |  - Do NOT join directly to sibling aggregate views (AGG) that are aggregated at a coarser grain unless you join on the aggregation keys exactly or re-aggregate this view to match. Example: joining track_sales_agg (if aggregated by TrackId) is safe only when joined on TrackId; joining an AGG aggregated by a different key (e.g., by AlbumId) requires re-aggregation or careful grouping. |  | Guidelines for correct composition: |  - To compute playlist-level measures (e.g., total sales for a playlist), first aggregate the sales table to TrackId -> metric (or to PlaylistId,TrackId if possible), then join that aggregated result to this view on TrackId (or PlaylistId+TrackId). This avoids duplicating playlist-track rows. |  - To compute distinct counts (e.g., distinct artists per playlist), aggregate this view: COUNT(DISTINCT ArtistId) GROUP BY PlaylistId. |  - To roll this view up to playlist-level metrics, GROUP BY PlaylistId (and optional playlist attributes like Playlist.Name). Do not join a one-to-many detail after grouping unless you re-aggregate the detail at the playlist key. |  | Examples of safe compositions: |  - Safe: this_view JOIN track_sales_agg ON track_sales_agg.TrackId = this_view.TrackId, if track_sales_agg is aggregated at TrackId — results in one row per playlist-track enriched with track-level sales. |  - Unsafe: this_view JOIN invoice_line ON invoice_line.TrackId = this_view.TrackId — invoice_line is many-per-track and will multiply rows; instead aggregate invoice_line to TrackId first (SUM(Quantity), SUM(UnitPrice*Quantity), etc.) then join.

views.description: Playlist-track membership enriched with track, album and artist names. Useful for playlist content inspection, playlist-based analytics, and export of playlist contents. | Use for: Show playlist contents with artist and album labels; Analyze popularity of tracks within playlists

views.name: employee_org_hierarchy
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.EmployeeId,
  e.FirstName,
  e.LastName,
  e.ReportsTo,
  0 AS Level,
  e.EmployeeId AS RootEmployeeId
FROM Employee e
UNION ALL
SELECT
  m.EmployeeId,
  m.FirstName,
  m.LastName,
  m.ReportsTo,
  eh.Level + 1 AS Level,
  eh.RootEmployeeId
FROM Employee m
JOIN employee_org_hierarchy eh ON m.EmployeeId = eh.ReportsTo

params.description: Recursive employee reporting hierarchy: each row is an employee as seen from a particular root employee and level (distance) in the reporting chain.
params.when_to_use: Find all managers (ancestors) or direct/indirect reports (descendants) for a given employee | Compute hierarchical relationships such as chain-of-command, depth from a root, or reporting path segments | Join to employee attributes or metrics at a given level of the org tree without duplicating aggregated measures (when respecting cardinality guidance) | As a building block to aggregate metrics up or down the org tree (e.g., rollup employee-level measures to a root manager)
params.output_schema: EmployeeId: unique identifier of the employee row in this view — derived from base table Employee.EmployeeId | FirstName: employee's first name — derived from base table Employee.FirstName | LastName: employee's last name — derived from base table Employee.LastName | ReportsTo: immediate manager's EmployeeId for this employee — derived from base table Employee.ReportsTo | Level: integer distance from the RootEmployeeId to this EmployeeId (0 means the row is the root employee itself) — computed in the recursive query as 0 for roots and eh.Level + 1 for each recursion | RootEmployeeId: the EmployeeId of the root employee from whose perspective the hierarchy row is produced — derived from base table Employee.EmployeeId in the anchor and carried through recursion
params.grounded_columns: Employee.EmployeeId | Employee.FirstName | Employee.LastName | Employee.ReportsTo | employee_org_hierarchy.ReportsTo | employee_org_hierarchy.Level | employee_org_hierarchy.RootEmployeeId
params.metric: Level = 0 (anchor) OR Level = previous.Level + 1 (recursive step) -- integer distance from RootEmployeeId to EmployeeId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to Employee (dimension) on Employee.EmployeeId = employee_org_hierarchy.EmployeeId — safe because Employee is one-row-per-EmployeeId and this view is already one-row-per (RootEmployeeId, EmployeeId, Level); joining preserves row uniqueness and does not duplicate this view's rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to customer_with_supportrep or other sibling views that are one-row-per-employee (e.g., support-rep metadata) on EmployeeId = <employee key in sibling> — safe when the sibling is one-row-per-employee because it won't multiply rows. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many detail/transaction tables or aggregate views that are one-to-many per EmployeeId (for example invoice_line_with_invoice_customer_track, track_sales_agg, monthly_invoice_totals, playlist_track_with_metadata, invoice_line_with_invoice_customer_track JOINs, or any raw invoice/invoice_line table) without re-aggregation or pre-aggregating the detail to the same grain as this view — such joins will multiply rows and thus duplicate measures. | If you need to combine this view with a one-to-many detail (sales, invoices, tracks), first aggregate the detail to the grouping (RootEmployeeId, EmployeeId, Level) or to EmployeeId (then join and aggregate by RootEmployeeId/Level as needed). Example safe pattern: aggregate invoice totals by Invoice.SupportRepId (or relevant employee key) producing one row per support rep, then join that aggregated result to employee_org_hierarchy on EmployeeId = SupportRepId and then further aggregate by RootEmployeeId/Level if desired. | When composing higher-level metrics (e.g., sum of sales under each RootEmployeeId), treat this view as a mapping from EmployeeId -> RootEmployeeId/Level. To avoid double-counting: (a) aggregate transactional data to EmployeeId before joining, or (b) join transactional data to EmployeeId and then GROUP BY RootEmployeeId/Level in the outer query. | Recursive-join note: the view's recursive definition already expands managers/trees; do not attempt to re-join employee_org_hierarchy to itself without a clear purpose and understanding of the intended additional expansion, as that can multiply rows beyond the intended (RootEmployeeId, EmployeeId, Level) granularity.

views.description: Recursive hierarchy of employees mapping each employee to their chain of managers (manager levels). Useful for org chart traversal, reporting line queries, and aggregated metrics up the management chain. | Use for: Find all reports (direct and indirect) for a manager; Aggregate metrics up managerial chains

views.name: tracks_ranked_by_sales
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.TrackId,
  t.Name,
  COALESCE(SUM(il.Quantity),0) AS TotalQuantitySold,
  COALESCE(SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity),0) AS TotalRevenue,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity),0) DESC) AS RevenueRank,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(SUM(il.Quantity),0) DESC) AS QuantityRank
FROM Track t
LEFT JOIN InvoiceLine il ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
GROUP BY t.TrackId, t.Name

params.description: Per-track sales totals and ranks: total quantity sold and total revenue per TrackId, with rank positions by revenue and by quantity.
params.when_to_use: Get total units sold and total revenue for each track (including tracks with zero sales). | Rank tracks by revenue or by quantity sold for leaderboards or top-N queries. | As a building block to compare track-level sales to other entities (album, artist, genre) by joining on TrackId, ensuring correct aggregation. | Filter or join top-ranked tracks into downstream analyses (e.g., top 10 revenue tracks) without recalculating base aggregates.
params.output_schema: TrackId: unique identifier of the track — derived from Track.TrackId (base column). | Name: track name/title — derived from Track.Name (base column). | TotalQuantitySold: total number of units sold for this track — derived as COALESCE(SUM(InvoiceLine.Quantity),0) aggregated per Track.TrackId. | TotalRevenue: total revenue for this track — derived as COALESCE(SUM(InvoiceLine.UnitPrice * InvoiceLine.Quantity),0) aggregated per Track.TrackId. | RevenueRank: rank (1 = highest) of the track by TotalRevenue — derived using RANK() window ordered by the aggregated TotalRevenue DESC. | QuantityRank: rank (1 = highest) of the track by TotalQuantitySold — derived using RANK() window ordered by the aggregated TotalQuantitySold DESC.
params.metric: TotalQuantitySold = COALESCE(SUM(InvoiceLine.Quantity), 0) grouped by Track.TrackId | TotalRevenue = COALESCE(SUM(InvoiceLine.UnitPrice * InvoiceLine.Quantity), 0) grouped by Track.TrackId | RevenueRank = RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(SUM(InvoiceLine.UnitPrice * InvoiceLine.Quantity), 0) DESC) computed over the grouped rows (TrackId partition implicit by GROUP BY) | QuantityRank = RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(SUM(InvoiceLine.Quantity), 0) DESC) computed over the grouped rows (TrackId partition implicit by GROUP BY)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to Track (base table) on TrackId — safe because this view is one row per TrackId and Track is one row per TrackId, so measures are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension-like sibling views that are also one-row-per-TrackId (for example, playlist_track_with_metadata if it is constrained to one row per TrackId) on TrackId — safe only if that sibling view is guaranteed one-row-per-TrackId. | do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many tables/views (for example InvoiceLine, playlist_track_with_metadata when it is one-to-many, or any raw invoice/invoice-line detail) without re-aggregation — joining a one-row-per-track aggregated view to a detail table with multiple rows per TrackId will multiply TotalQuantitySold and TotalRevenue and invalidate the measures. | When combining with higher-grain aggregates (e.g., album- or artist-level aggregations), either: (a) join this view to an album/artist dimension on TrackId and then SUM(TotalRevenue) grouped by AlbumId/ArtistId (safe because summing pre-aggregated per-track measures yields correct album/artist totals), or (b) join album/artist to underlying invoice lines and re-aggregate from invoice lines directly. Prefer method (a) when you want to reuse these precomputed per-track measures. | Do NOT join this view to another aggregated view that is at track-level but expanded by additional one-to-many relationships (e.g., a view that replicates tracks per-playlist or per-invoice without collapsing) without first collapsing the other side to one row per TrackId; otherwise the track-level measures will be duplicated. | Safe pattern examples: (1) To get album totals: join tracks_ranked_by_sales on TrackId to a track->album mapping that is one-row-per-TrackId, then SUM(TotalRevenue) GROUP BY AlbumId. (2) To attach artist metadata: join on Track.TrackId to a view providing ArtistId per TrackId (one row per TrackId) and aggregate the track measures by ArtistId. | Unsafe pattern examples: (1) Joining tracks_ranked_by_sales directly to InvoiceLine on TrackId to compute further metrics — unsafe because InvoiceLine has many rows per TrackId and would multiply the aggregated measures. (2) Joining to playlist_track_with_metadata when that view contains multiple rows per TrackId (one per playlist) — unsafe unless playlist side is first aggregated to one row per TrackId.

views.description: Tracks ranked by revenue and quantity sold using window functions. Exposes rank values so callers can filter top-N downstream. Useful for top-K queries without embedding a literal top-K in the CTE. | Use for: Top-N tracks by revenue or quantity (downstream WHERE RevenueRank <= k); Compare rank by quantity vs revenue

views.name: customer_lifetime_value
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Customer.CustomerId,
  Customer.FirstName,
  Customer.LastName,
  COUNT(DISTINCT Invoice.InvoiceId) AS InvoiceCount,
  SUM(Invoice.Total) AS TotalRevenue,
  MIN(Invoice.InvoiceDate) AS FirstInvoiceDate,
  MAX(Invoice.InvoiceDate) AS LastInvoiceDate,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT Invoice.InvoiceId) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE SUM(Invoice.Total) / COUNT(DISTINCT Invoice.InvoiceId) END AS AvgInvoiceValue
FROM Customer
LEFT JOIN Invoice ON Customer.CustomerId = Invoice.CustomerId
GROUP BY Customer.CustomerId, Customer.FirstName, Customer.LastName

params.description: Per-customer lifetime metrics: counts and revenue from all invoices per customer (one row per CustomerId).
params.when_to_use: Get lifetime value and invoice activity for each customer (e.g., reporting CLV, first/last purchase dates). | Join a customer-level result to customer attributes or dimensions (one-to-one) without re-aggregation. | Use as a base for customer-level segmentation, cohorts, or input to models that require per-customer aggregates. | Compose higher-level aggregates (e.g., total revenue by sales rep or country) by aggregating this view on CustomerId or joining safely to one-row-per-customer dimensions.
params.output_schema: CustomerId: unique identifier for the customer — sourced from Customer.CustomerId (grouping key). | FirstName: customer's first name — sourced from Customer.FirstName (grouping column, repeated per CustomerId). | LastName: customer's last name — sourced from Customer.LastName (grouping column, repeated per CustomerId). | InvoiceCount: number of distinct invoices for the customer — derived as COUNT(DISTINCT Invoice.InvoiceId) over invoices joined to the customer. | TotalRevenue: total revenue for the customer — derived as SUM(Invoice.Total) over invoices joined to the customer (nulls treated as 0 only if SQL engine does so; SUM over zero rows yields NULL in some engines, but here LEFT JOIN+GROUP gives NULL or 0 depending on engine; original SQL returns SUM(Invoice.Total)). | FirstInvoiceDate: date of the customer's earliest invoice — derived as MIN(Invoice.InvoiceDate). | LastInvoiceDate: date of the customer's latest invoice — derived as MAX(Invoice.InvoiceDate). | AvgInvoiceValue: average invoice value for the customer — derived as SUM(Invoice.Total) / COUNT(DISTINCT Invoice.InvoiceId), with a CASE to return NULL when InvoiceCount = 0.
params.grounded_columns: Customer.CustomerId | Customer.FirstName | Customer.LastName | Invoice.InvoiceId | Invoice.Total | Invoice.InvoiceDate | Invoice.CustomerId
params.metric: InvoiceCount = COUNT(DISTINCT Invoice.InvoiceId)  -- distinct count of invoices per CustomerId | TotalRevenue = SUM(Invoice.Total)  -- sum of Invoice.Total for invoices with matching CustomerId | FirstInvoiceDate = MIN(Invoice.InvoiceDate)  -- earliest InvoiceDate for the customer | LastInvoiceDate = MAX(Invoice.InvoiceDate)  -- latest InvoiceDate for the customer | AvgInvoiceValue = CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT Invoice.InvoiceId) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE SUM(Invoice.Total) / COUNT(DISTINCT Invoice.InvoiceId) END  -- average revenue per invoice for the customer
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to customer dimension tables or one-row-per-customer views on CustomerId — safe because this view is one row per CustomerId so its measures (InvoiceCount, TotalRevenue, AvgInvoiceValue) will not be duplicated. Example: join to customer_with_supportrep on CustomerId (one-to-one) because that view is keyed by CustomerId. | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views on CustomerId (for example: invoice_line_with_invoice_customer_track or playlist_track_with_metadata) without re-aggregating the right-hand side first, because such joins will multiply rows per CustomerId and therefore inflate InvoiceCount and TotalRevenue. Instead, aggregate the many-side to customer-level measures and then join. | Safe composition pattern to roll-up to other dims: to compute totals by support rep, first join customer_lifetime_value (one row per CustomerId) to customer_with_supportrep (one row per CustomerId) on CustomerId, then aggregate TotalRevenue by SupportRepId. This preserves correctness because joins are one-to-one on CustomerId. | If joining to another AGG view (e.g., artist_album_counts) ensure the other view is also at one-row-per-key and that the join key represents a true one-to-one relationship. If the other side is one-to-many, re-aggregate the other side to CustomerId (or to the target grain) before joining. | When composing into higher-level aggregates (e.g., monthly or regional totals), aggregate this view's TotalRevenue and InvoiceCount after joining any customer-level attributes that are one-row-per-customer; do not sum after joining to tables that introduce multiplicity without first de-duplicating or aggregating.

views.description: Customer-level revenue and purchase metrics: total revenue, total invoices, first and last invoice dates, average invoice value. Useful for CLV, segmentation, and retention analysis. | Use for: Customer lifetime value and recency/frequency/monetary (RFM) features; Identify high-value customers for marketing

views.name: track_basic_duration
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  TrackId,
  AlbumId,
  Name,
  Milliseconds,
  (Milliseconds / 60000.0) AS Minutes
FROM track_with_album_artist_genre_media
WHERE Milliseconds IS NOT NULL
views.description: One row per track with canonical duration in milliseconds and minutes, and key track metadata (ids and linking columns). Null durations are excluded by default to simplify downstream aggregations.

views.name: track_invoice_revenue_lines
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  InvoiceLine.InvoiceLineId AS InvoiceLineId,
  InvoiceLine.InvoiceId AS InvoiceId,
  InvoiceLine.TrackId AS TrackId,
  InvoiceLine.UnitPrice AS UnitPrice,
  InvoiceLine.Quantity AS Quantity,
  (InvoiceLine.UnitPrice * InvoiceLine.Quantity) AS LineRevenue
FROM InvoiceLine
JOIN Invoice USING(InvoiceId)
JOIN Track USING(TrackId)
WHERE InvoiceLine.UnitPrice IS NOT NULL
  AND InvoiceLine.Quantity IS NOT NULL
views.description: Invoice line level revenue joined to track key so revenue can be aggregated by any track attribute. Excludes invoice lines with NULL UnitPrice or NULL Quantity to avoid ambiguous revenue.

views.name: track_duration_stats_dataset
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  MIN(Milliseconds) AS MinMilliseconds,
  AVG(Milliseconds) AS AvgMilliseconds,
  MAX(Milliseconds) AS MaxMilliseconds,
  MIN(Milliseconds) / 60000.0 AS MinMinutes,
  AVG(Milliseconds) / 60000.0 AS AvgMinutes,
  MAX(Milliseconds) / 60000.0 AS MaxMinutes
FROM Track
WHERE Milliseconds IS NOT NULL
views.description: Dataset-wide duration statistics computed from Track rows with non-null Milliseconds: min, avg, max (in milliseconds) and their equivalents in minutes. Useful to derive category boundaries that depend on dataset-wide min/avg/max.

views.name: track_basic_duration_13
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.TrackId AS TrackId,
  t.Milliseconds AS Milliseconds,
  (CAST(t.Milliseconds AS REAL) / 60000.0) AS DurationMinutes,
  t.AlbumId AS AlbumId
FROM Track t
views.description: One row per Track with canonical duration in minutes as a floating-point value and basic track identifiers and album/artist references for joins.

views.name: track_category_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.TrackId,
  (t.Milliseconds / 60000.0) AS DurationMinutes,
  CASE
    WHEN t.Milliseconds <= (s.MinMilliseconds + (s.AvgMilliseconds - s.MinMilliseconds) / 2.0) THEN 'Short'
    WHEN t.Milliseconds <= (s.AvgMilliseconds + (s.MaxMilliseconds - s.AvgMilliseconds) / 2.0) THEN 'Medium'
    ELSE 'Long'
  END AS Category
FROM track_basic_duration_13 t
CROSS JOIN track_duration_stats_dataset s
views.description: Assigns each track to a duration category ('Short','Medium','Long') using dataset-wide min/avg/max breakpoints (midpoints m1 and m2). This view expects the dataset-wide stats to be supplied or computed when materializing the view; it is one row per track with its computed category.

views.name: invoice_line_revenue_by_track
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  TrackId AS TrackId,
  SUM(UnitPrice * Quantity) AS TotalRevenue,
  COUNT(*) AS InvoiceLineCount
FROM InvoiceLine
GROUP BY TrackId
views.description: Aggregated revenue and invoice-line counts per Track by summing UnitPrice * Quantity on InvoiceLine. One row per TrackId with raw revenue measure for joining to track cohorts.
